clue.text: Plant, when frost comes, loses head

indicators.note: losing its head means the season word drops its first letter

parts.note: frost comes in the cold season, winter

explanation.surface: A garden plant dies back once the frost arrives and loses its flowering top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' takes the W off WINTER. 'Plant' is the verb here: to bury, as you would a body.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury in the ground, just as one plants a seed or a corpse.

parts.note: a woolly jumper is a sheep; the one counting sheep is someone who cannot sleep

explanation.surface: A knitwear shop's sales counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot sleep, traditionally counting sheep jumping a fence.

parts.note: hide means skin, so pictures on hide are inked designs on skin

explanation.surface: Someone whose work is concealing paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist's trade is inking pictures into the skin.

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: wrapt is an old spelling of wrapped, meaning packaged

explanation.surface: A parcel was wrapped and shipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means carried away, enraptured, transported with delight.

parts.note: an angel is an ideal, perfect person, and a fish is a swimmer; together they name a tropical aquarium fish

explanation.surface: Praise for a flawless competitor in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical reef fish whose name joins a word for a perfect person with a word for a swimming creature.

clue.text: Initiate march another way-one has to handle numbers

indicators.note: another way tells us to arrange these letters differently

explanation.surface: Organisers start a march by a different route, someone dealing with the headcount.
explanation.definitionFit: An arithmetician is an expert in calculation who works with numbers.

definitions.meaning: a crescent moon shape, from the French for moon
a river in north-west England flowing through Lancaster

explanation.definitionFit: A lune is a crescent-shaped figure, and the Lune is a river in Lancashire.

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: the yellow flag is a kind of iris

explanation.surface: A country's banner flies above a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the plant, the yellow flag iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish describes someone of Ireland's nationality.

definitions.meaning: a small gummed strip used to fix a stamp into an album
the pivot on which a door, or figuratively an argument, swings

explanation.definitionFit: A stamp hinge is a mount, and a hinge is what something turns on.

parts.note: a set is a unit of play in tennis
to be up is to be ahead, in the lead

explanation.surface: A player tries to build an early advantage in a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up a business or system is to establish it.

parts.note: a flash of creative thought, and also the name of a short contrapuntal keyboard piece, as in Bach's two-part works

explanation.surface: A composer's sudden idea for a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A creative brainwave is an invention, and Bach wrote keyboard pieces called inventions.

parts.note: spots offering a wide outlook, and also what a tennis umpire perched high above the court calls when a player gains the lead after deuce

explanation.surface: The general opinions of a senior judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Places offering a commanding view, punned on tennis scoring points of advantage.

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A singer is asked to take the deep note normally given to the tenor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tenor' looks musical but means general drift or feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of a meeting is its general character or atmosphere.

clue.text: King's companion in tip of Kent, mainly

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, here losing its final letter

parts.note: the Isle of Thanet forms the north-eastern tip of the English county of Kent

explanation.surface: A royal attendant is found at the far end of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: THANET is the north-eastern corner of Kent, a county in south-east England; 'mainly' drops its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Saxon and Scottish history a thane was a nobleman holding land in the king's service.

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken old-fashioned Irish accent is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brogue' suggests an Irish accent, but here it is a stout leather shoe; 'possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a sturdy decorated leather shoe, one example of footwear.
Steep means overpriced, and to steep food is to soak or marinate it.

clue.text: Civic Centre on Back Lane is for sale

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A civic centre stands on a lane behind the high street and is up for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' picks V from Civic; 'Back' turns LANE into ENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Venal means open to bribery, willing to sell influence.

clue.text: As shipmates are, sharing rough passage?

definitions.text: As shipmates are, sharing rough passage?

parts.words: As shipmates are, sharing rough passage?
parts.note: people on one vessel share a stormy crossing; the idiom means sharing a common difficulty

explanation.surface: Crew members endure a stormy voyage together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sharing the same difficult situation, as literal shipmates do.

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Cattle charge out of some rough taverns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' is part of the fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Onrushing means rushing forward headlong, as a stampede does.

clue.text: Like Figaro's work taking on so in ordeal

indicators.note: in places one set of letters inside another

parts.note: a trial is an ordeal

explanation.surface: Figaro takes on a difficult task and so endures an ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Figaro is the barber of Seville in the operas by Rossini and Mozart.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsorial means relating to barbers or hairdressing, Figaro's trade.

clue.text: Royal wife in rare chapter of settlement

indicators.note: a settlement is an arrangement, so the preceding letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A queen consort appears in an unusual chapter about a land settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth and final wife of Henry VIII, who outlived him.

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, plus the S of the possessive
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A firm delivers a tough blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosh someone is to strike them with a heavy bludgeon.

clue.text: Roman god, in court, held by police

indicators.note: held by puts one piece inside another

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police
to be up before a judge is to be in court

explanation.surface: A deity is put on trial and kept in custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid is the Roman god of love.

clue.text: Wheat stalks bring up skin blemishes

indicators.note: in a down clue, bring up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: warts are skin blemishes

explanation.surface: Contact with harvested wheat raises marks on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw is the dried stalks of wheat or other cereal.

parts.note: reads as slightly astray, but means a piece of turf hacked off a golf course

explanation.surface: Something has strayed a little from its planned route.
explanation.definitionFit: A divot is the lump of turf a golf club cuts from the ground.

clue.text: Capital consists of mainly loose change

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters
mainly means most of the word, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A city's wealth is said to be mostly small coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims LOOSE to LOOS, and 'change' rearranges those letters. 'loose change' reads as coins, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Church volunteers come up for informal talk

indicators.note: in a down clue, come up means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Church helpers arrive for a casual conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the UK volunteer reserve; 'come up' turns it to AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is a casual, informal conversation.

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
an air is a manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: A couple have a quiet, reserved manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a couple, two of a kind.

clue.text: Standard, at that time, advanced to build great temple

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
then means at that time
on means advanced or forward

explanation.surface: A normal plan of that era was pushed forward to construct a huge shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the great temple of Athena on the Athenian Acropolis.

clue.text: I get bail, perhaps, with this excuse

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A suspect hopes their story will get them released on bail.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as an excuse.

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
turns are acts or performances on stage

explanation.surface: A county's performers start to fade.
explanation.walkthrough: DOWN is a county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Downturns are declines in activity or fortune, as in the economy.

parts.note: to rig is to equip or fit out
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Instructions to fit out a huge Spanish figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigel is a blue supergiant star, the brightest in Orion.
